summary: Yaroslav Komarovski works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at traditional institutions under teachers including Lobsang Gyatso and at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins and others. He held a postdoctoral fellowship at Washington University and a post at the University of Nebraska-Lincoln.

Yaroslav Vasilkov is an Indologist who studied at the Faculty of Oriental Studies of St. Petersburg University (circa 1961–1967). He held posts at the Saint Petersburg Academy of Sciences (~1974–2005), Saint Petersburg State University (~1990), and Kunstkamera (~2005).

Yasuaki Nara (1929–2017) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Hajime Nakamura and Kogen Mizuno, and at the University of Calcutta. He served at Komazawa University from 1960 and directed the Soto Zen Research Center in 2000.

Yasuhiko Nagano is a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics. He studied at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies, the University of Tokyo, and UC Berkeley (Ph.D. 1975–1983). He was a professor at the National Museum of Ethnology and vice president of SOKENDAI (2011–2014).
Yasuhiko Sueki is a scholar of philosophy and Sinology who studied at the University of Tokyo. He served as professor emeritus at Komazawa University around 2018.

Yasuhiro Okazaki works in Indology and philosophy. He earned his PhD at Hiroshima University under Atsushi Uno, Shoryu Katsura, and Hiroakira Ono, and held posts at Chiyoda High School, Hiroshima Prefectural Kabe High School, and Hiroshima Prefectural Takamiya High School.

Yasuhiro Sueki is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who completed short-term study under George Baumann at Tübingen University Library. He served as a senior research fellow at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (~1996–2021) and at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Yasuhiro Tsuchiyama is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who is attested as a lecturer at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies in 2026.
Yasuhiro Ueno is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral studies at Kyoto University (attested 2003–2004). He held posts at Kyoto University and Koyasan University (attested 2004).

Yasuhiro Yamazaki (1929–2025) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Koyasan University (~1950–1954). He served as an assistant professor at Shuchiin University (1966–2000) and as a professor at Koyasan University (~1978–2000).

Yasuke Ikari is an Indologist who studied at Kyoto University and the University of Chicago (PhD ~1968–1973). He held appointments at Kyoto University (assistant 1973, associate professor 1982 and 1986–1990, professor emeritus 2004), Kindai University (1978), and the National Museum of Ethnology (1979).

Yasuko Kojima is a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics who is attested in 2026 as a lecturer at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Yasumasa Sekine is a religious studies and Indology scholar educated at Tokyo Institute of Technology and SOAS. His main posts include assistant at Tokyo Institute of Technology, associate professor at Tsukuba, and professor at Japan Women's University (~1999–2015) and Kwansei Gakuin University (~2015–2020).

Yasunori Ejima (1939–1999) was an Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his degrees at the University of Tokyo. He held posts at the Institute for Advanced Studies on Asia (1966–1974) and the University of Tokyo, becoming professor in 1987.

Yasuo Deguchi is a philosophy and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University. He held posts at Nagoya Institute of Technology and Kyoto University, where he became professor in 2016 and dean (2023–2025), and founded the Kyoto Institute of Philosophy in 2023.
Yasuo Goto is a Buddhist studies scholar who held lecturing positions at Ryukoku University (attested 1991 and 2006) and Shuchiin University (attested 2006).
Yasuo Inamoto is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He held a post as a technical official at Nara National Museum (~1993–2002) and joined Kyoto University around 2002.

Yasuo Matsunami (1948–2010) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Taisho University under Ryukai Mano and later served there as a lecturer (attested 1992–2006), as well as advisor to the Śrāvakabhūmi Study Group until 2010.
Yasuo Sano is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Kenyu Mitomo (attested 1996) and founded the Buha Bukkyo Shiso Kenkyukai.

Yasuo Yuasa (1925–2005) was a scholar of philosophy and religious studies who studied at the University of Tokyo under Tetsuro Watsuji. He held faculty posts at the University of Yamanashi, Osaka University, and the University of Tsukuba (1981–1989).
